meta.notes: POST /webhook/notifications {action:'list'|'mark_read', campaign_id, limit?, since?, ids?, all?} - Feed behind the SPOTTER header ticker. On 'list' it takes a rate-limited lease and sweeps the campaign graph for anything new (high-value attack paths from WF04, C2 agent status transitions, FlareBreach records, enricher alert tags, open CloudAsset buckets from WF13), then returns the newest notifications with per-operator read state. No producer workflow emits into this - the sweep derives everything from nodes those workflows already write, so WF01/04/09/13/21 are untouched. Storage is (:SpotterMeta:SpotterNotification) nodes: dual-labelled so WF07's orphan sweep (guarded AND NOT n:SpotterMeta) cannot delete the feed, and carrying NO sketch_id so an unresolvable nodeType can never 500 a sketch. sketch_id is derived from the campaign registry, never from the request body, so one operator cannot sweep another's graph. Returns {notifications:[{id,ts,kind,severity,title,detail,target_label,target_kind,target_id,campaign_id,read}], unread, swept, created, generated_at, errors}. All logic lives in scripts/spotter_notify.py.

parameters.pythonCode:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/data/scripts')

# Hard import on purpose. spotter_notify is on the runner's import allowlist
# (N8N_RUNNERS_EXTERNAL_ALLOW in n8n-task-runners.json) and is mounted at
# /data/scripts, so a failure here is a real deployment fault and should be
# loud rather than silently serving an empty feed forever.
import spotter_notify as notify

# Everything after the import is defensive. This endpoint is polled once a
# minute by every open browser, so a runtime fault has to degrade to an empty
# feed -- a 500 here would paint an error across the header of every operator's
# dashboard, which is worse than showing no news. handle() already swallows its
# own errors and reports them in `errors`; this is the backstop for the ones it
# cannot anticipate.
try:
    result = notify.handle(_items)
except Exception as exc:
    result = {
        'notifications': [],
        'unread': 0,
        'errors': [str(exc)[:200].replace('\n', ' ')],
    }

return [{'json': result}]
